summary: Yukihiro Okada is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. Okada held posts at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College and Minobusan University.
Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) was a Japanese history and archaeology scholar who studied at Ritsumeikan University from around 1954 to 1964 and later held a post there from around 1970 to 2001.

Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University from around 1952 to 1956 and held a post at Japan Women's University from around 1972 to 1980.
Yukio Kotani (born 1931) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. He held a post as an emeritus professor at Rissho University from around 1970 to 2002.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held positions at Toyo University and Rissho University, including president.

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1963). He held posts at Nagoya City University, Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (~1981–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.

Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Freiburg, Yamanaka has held posts at the University of Göttingen and Ryukoku University's Research Center for World Buddhist Culture.

Yuko Kamishima works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, as well as under Ekai Kawaguchi, before serving at Waseda University and Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an attested post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College in 2001.

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She has served as an associate professor at Kyoto University.
Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under supervisor Kirill Solonin and traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo.
Yumi Nakamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at Ryukoku University and held a research post there in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from around 1980 to 1989 and held a post there around 1999.

Yumin Dai works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Dai studied at Hebei University, Nanjing University, and the University of Arizona, and was appointed assistant professor at Nanjing University in 2019.

Yumzhana Zhabon specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1979 to 1985 and became a senior researcher at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies in 1985.
Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at Fudan University by 2006 and held an attested post as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore in 2015.

Yung-Jong Shiah works in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at the University of Edinburgh (2003–2008). In 2025, Shiah was appointed Chair Professor and Dean of the College of Buddhist Studies at Fo Guang University.
Yungfen Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at Columbia University, studying under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.
Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a Sinologist who studied at Fudan University from around 1944 to 1948 and subsequently held a post there from around 1948 to 2004.
